A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OKGQA/OKGQA-P study. All 18 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison; relocated text, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM comparisons on OKGQA and experiments with four KG perturbation methods on OKGQA-P, including Table 2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original human–LLM correlation and inter-rater agreement results in Appendix A.2, Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The two-hop/PPR graph construction, prize-cost triplet and path retrieval, PCST subgraph retrieval, and graph-guided generation remain the same. Expanded explanations, including the relation-replacement rationale, do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 850 OKGQA queries, 816 DBpedia entities, ten query subtypes and four OKGQA-P perturbation types. The new annotation analyses assess existing benchmark construction without adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same five LLMs and comparator membership across zero-shot, four-shot, CoT, CoT+SC and KG retrieval variants. Newly cited works such as Fidelis and UniGraph are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a validation protocol comparing human and LLM query-quality scores across four refinement rounds and agreement between evaluator pairs. The original QA metrics, model configurations, two-hop extraction and perturbation settings are retained; the newly disclosed annotator count does not establish increased recruitment.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 add supplementary checks of whether iterative refinement improves human–LLM alignment and whether human query-quality judgments are consistent. Existing retrieval-form, query-type and KG perturbation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 first reports Pearson correlations and pairwise Cohen's kappa for query annotation. Table 2's existing plus/minus reporting is unchanged, and no increase in repeated model runs or new seed information is reported.

E6.justification: All 216 mean-and-error pairs in Table 2 and the corresponding performance plots are unchanged. New Table 3 reports, for example, naturalness correlation increasing from 0.60 to 0.74 across rounds; Table 4 adds pairwise kappa values ranging from 0.58 to 0.85.

T1.justification: The likelihood equations, retrieval scores, PPR equation and ATS/SC2D/SD2 definitions retain their mathematical substance. The explicit argmax for Z* restates v1's most-probable-retrieval approximation. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the OKGQA/OKGQA-P contributions and principal findings about KG augmentation, internal reasoning and subgraph retrieval. Rewritten motivation and removal of the contribution bullets do not materially change these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning DBpedia's suitability for specialized domains and the assumption of static KGs. It also interprets annotation agreement and subjectivity, and expands explanations for two-hop extraction and relation-replacement negatives.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies three fluent-English, computer-science annotators and adds a JSON query example. It removes the worked blockchain generation example and v1's stated edge-cost default of 1. The abstract now explicitly mentions data alongside code at the same repository link.

R1.justification: Eight cited works are added, covering open-ended evaluation, annotation agreement and graph research, including OpenCQA, LongHalQA, Landis and Koch, Fidelis and UniGraph. The existing survey and central positioning around open-ended KGQA are largely retained.

P1.justification: The document is substantially rewritten and reorganized: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Appendix B, evaluation metrics move into Experiments, and appendices are regrouped into A–C. The introduction, benchmark overview and conclusion are revised, prompts are condensed, and author/header text changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively relocating and resizing displays. v2 adds the motivating Figure 1, Tables 3–4 and the JSON example in Figure 8, rearranges the framework diagram, and adds row shading to Table 2. Existing result plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: v1 describes human-guided query construction without reporting agreement evidence; v2's Tables 3–4 provide useful validation, while its new limitations better qualify applicability. These are modest gains despite unchanged primary results. Benefits are tempered by omitted implementation details and an inconsistency: the novelty-kappa discussion states 0.61–0.63, whereas Table 4 reports 0.58–0.61.
